newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador unions extend walkout to indefinite strike.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador unions extend walkout to indefinite strike.

text.p: Ecuador's militant trade unions, which launched a 48-hour general strike Wednesday, said on Thursday that workers would stay out indefinitely, or until President Abdala Bucaram was dismissed.

"In a meeting at dawn, we decided to harden our stance and continue the strike until we achieve the dismissal of Abdala Bucaram," the Coordinating Board for Social Protests and the Indigenous Peoples Confederation said in a statement.
Thousands of workers took to the streets Wednesday heeding the strike and urging Congress to remove Bucaram from office for his austerity policies and extravagant behaviour.
Support for the strike was unclear. But industry, commerce and public transport were halted in major cities and government offices were closed around the country. Oil production, however, was normal.

"Close to two million people of indigneous background or belonging to the Farmers Social Insurance group will continue to man the roadblocks that went up Monday in coastal, mountainous and western areas," the board's statement said.
In Quito, hundreds of protesters surrounded the Congress building awaiting a special afternoon session called to debate the possibility of ousting Bucaram.
